title: Chemical Engineer (Core)
summary: Chemical engineers design and run processes that turn raw materials into fuels, chemicals, medicines and food. This path suits students who like balances, thermodynamics and simulating a plant before it is built.

sources.title: GATE 2027 Chemical Engineering (CH) syllabus – IIT Madras
DWSIM – A Chemical Process Simulator – FOSSEE

nodes.title: Process calculations: material and energy balances
nodes.summary: Learn units, single and multi-unit material balances, recycle and bypass, reactions and energy balances. This is the language of every chemical plant and the first CH topic in GATE.

resources.title: Material & Energy Balance Computations – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)

nodes.proof: Solved notes for 25+ balance problems, including at least five with recycle or reaction.

sources.title: Material & Energy Balance Computations – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)

nodes.title: Chemical engineering thermodynamics
nodes.summary: Learn equations of state, solution thermodynamics, phase equilibria and reaction equilibria. You need these to choose the right property model in a simulator and to answer interview questions.
nodes.proof: A worked vapour-liquid equilibrium (VLE) example for a binary mixture, with a hand-drawn or plotted T-x-y diagram.

nodes.title: Process simulation with DWSIM
nodes.summary: DWSIM is a free, open-source process simulator. Learn to set up components, property packages, streams and unit operations using the FOSSEE spoken tutorials.

resources.title: DWSIM – A Chemical Process Simulator – FOSSEE

nodes.proof: A DWSIM file for a simple flash or distillation column, with a screenshot and a note on why you chose the property package.

sources.title: DWSIM – A Chemical Process Simulator – FOSSEE

nodes.title: Chemical process safety
nodes.summary: Learn the basics of toxicology, fires and explosions, relief systems, HAZOP and risk assessment. Plants take safety very seriously, and interviewers often ask about HAZOP.
nodes.proof: A small HAZOP table (nodes, deviations, causes, safeguards) for one unit of your flowsheet.

nodes.title: FOSSEE DWSIM flowsheeting project
nodes.summary: Recreate a real process flowsheet from a textbook or journal in DWSIM through the FOSSEE flowsheeting project. Reviewed submissions get a FOSSEE internship e-certificate.
nodes.proof: A completed flowsheet (more than two unit operations) with a short report comparing your results to the source.

nodes.title: Join IIChE as a student member
nodes.summary: Undergraduate chemical engineering students can become IIChE student members, usually through a college student chapter. Chapter events are a good way to meet working engineers.
nodes.proof: Student membership or chapter role, and one event you attended or helped run, summarised in a short note.

nodes.title: GATE CH and PSU recruitment
nodes.summary: Oil and gas PSUs such as GAIL and IndianOil have hired chemical engineers using GATE CH scores. Use the official syllabus and past papers, and read each PSU advertisement for eligibility.
nodes.proof: Three full past CH papers solved under time limits, with a topic-wise error log.

nodes.title: Interview and placement preparation
nodes.summary: Revise core subjects with past GATE questions, practise explaining your flowsheet and HAZOP, and work on group discussion and interview skills. PSU selection often adds a GD and interview after GATE.
nodes.proof: Two mock interviews done with a senior or faculty member, and a one-page résumé listing your DWSIM project.
